summary: In Greek mythology, Agrius (Ancient Greek Ἄγριος, "wild") is one of the earthborn Giants. In Apollodorus' Gigantomachy the Moirai club him and Thoon to death with brazen maces while the Olympians and Heracles fight the rest of the brood.
etymology: Greek Ἄγριος (Ágrios), "wild, savage," from agros ("field / wild land").
cultCenters: Cosmic battlefield of the Gigantomachy (no civic cult)

sections.heading: Giant of the Gigantomachy
paragraphs: Apollodorus names Agrius among Gaia's giant sons who assault Olympus. While Zeus, Athena, and the other gods fight with Heracles' aid, the Fates kill Agrius and Thoon with clubs of bronze — a rare starring role for the Moirai in open battle.
The collective node gigantes holds the revolt and the disputed parentage of the brood; this node is the individual named in that roster.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: Wikipedia's Agrius page also lists Agrius son of Porthaon at Calydon, a centaur, a Circean son of Odysseus, a suitor of Penelope, and others. The atlas id agrius-giant with kinds giant is only the Gigantomachy fighter.
